title: Backoff Prober + Idempotency Reconciliation: SDK Observability & Cross-Language Ergonomics
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Summary: Add a lightweight 'backoff prober' layer across Python/TS/Go SDKs that uses runtime telemetry to pick conservative default retry/backoff profiles, surface idempotency reconciliation events, and provide language-native ergonomic helpers for streaming resume and dedupe keys. This ticket codifies API ergonomics, observability signals, experiment plan, and provides cross-lang snippets for adoption.

Goals:
- Provide safer defaults that reduce duplicate work/charges while preserving high-success rate for transient errors.
- Emit standardized telemetry when the SDK suppresses retries or drops a resume window so the platform can detect systematic failures.
- Make idempotency key reconciliation obvious and easy in both request-based and streaming calls.
- Ensure consistent behavior and docs across Python/TS/Go with minimal breaking changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDKs expose a BackoffProber config with three knobs (sensitivity, early_fail_threshold_ms, budget_window_seconds) documented and covered by unit tests.
- SDK emits telemetry events: sdk.retry.probed, sdk.retry.early_fail, sdk.idempotency.reconcile with schema fields (stringified as flat attributes in telemetry).
- Examples and migration guide added to the SDK repo with runnable snippets for Python/TS/Go.
- Runtime experiment (10k requests per SDK) shows <=10% token-cost increase for success-optimized workloads and >=40% reduction in duplicate requests for burst failure patterns.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Adaptive probing vs fixed profiles: we opt for adaptive probing with a conservative cold-start profile to avoid large burst costs on first requests. The prober collects short windows of latency/error percentiles and flips to faster backoff only after a stable success signal. Trade-off: slightly higher latency on initial requests for fewer duplicates.
- Early-fail heuristic: if the SDK detects client-side budget exhaustion (per-request estimated-cost > budget_window), it will fail fast with a transient-failure hint to the app to avoid cascading retries. This preserves customer billing predictability at the cost of more visible client errors in pathological situations.
- Idempotency reconciliation: for streaming/resumable flows we attach an id_key token to each chunk; if the server returns a resume token mismatch we emit sdk.idempotency.reconcile with suggested next steps (retry with new id_key or abort). We do not automatically rotate id_keys to avoid hidden semantics.

API ergonomic proposals (per language):
- Python (recommended): BackoffProber as optional field on ClientConfig. Exposes context-manager helper for streaming that returns an IdempotencyHandle with .resume_from(token) and .rotate_key(new_key).
  Example:
  
  from redwood import Client, BackoffProberConfig
  cfg = BackoffProberConfig(sensitivity=0.6, early_fail_threshold_ms=120, budget_window_seconds=30)
  client = Client(api_key=..., backoff_prober=cfg)

  with client.streaming_idempotency("chat_stream") as handle:
      for chunk in handle.stream(prompt):
          ...

- TypeScript: BackoffProber added to client options; streaming helper returns an AsyncIterable with events {type: 'chunk'|'resume'|'reconcile'}. The TS helper emits a 'reconcile' event when idempotency mismatch occurs so apps can present UI or retry.

- Go: BackoffProber as functional option on NewClient(...). Streaming API returns a struct {C <-chan Chunk, Reconcile <-chan ReconcileEvent} so developers can select on channels. Keep pattern idiomatic to Go with minimal GC overhead.

Telemetry & instrumentation:
- Emit event sdk.retry.probed {language, profile, sensitivity, probe_window_ms}.
- Emit event sdk.retry.early_fail {reason, estimated_cost_tokens, threshold_tokens}.
- Emit event sdk.idempotency.reconcile {operation, id_key_in_use, server_resume_token, suggested_action}.
- All events include: sdk_version, runtime_os, request_route, model, region, and a monotonic-event-id.
- Backend: events will land in existing telemetry pipeline (Snowplow/Datadog) with a dashboard that shows per-route duplicate-rate, early-fail-rate, and idempotency-reconcile-rate.

Testing & validation plan:
- Unit tests that simulate transient 503/429 patterns and assert that the prober adapts within N probes.
- Integration test against a flaky local server that returns resume-mismatches to assert idempotency.reconcile emitted and client does not silently rotate keys.
- Canary rollout: 5% of SDK traffic with feature flag, monitor duplicate-rate and error-surface.

Rollout and rollout gating:
- Feature behind server-side opt-in and client default disabled for existing major versions. New SDK minor release enables the prober with conservative default.
- Gate metrics: if duplicate_rate decreases and early_fail_rate < 0.5% and user-error-rate does not increase by >25% we progressively expand rollout.

Docs & migration:
- Add a migration doc linking to sample snippets, explain rationale and how to opt-out (client.disable_backoff_prober=True).
- Provide a troubleshooting checklist for when apps see increased early-fails (inspect telemetry, increase sensitivity, widen budget_window_seconds).

Open questions (for review):
- Should auto-rotation of id_keys be offered as an opt-in convenience? (Pros: fewer manual steps for apps; Cons: hidden semantics cause debugging difficulty.)
- Exact telemetry schema fields to include in the first pass (we propose the minimal set above).

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SDK/pages/BR-BackoffProber
- API PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1421
- Telemetry dashboard mock: https://datadog.com/dash/redwood/backoff-prober-mock
- Benchmark harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/tree/main/backoff-prober

Next steps:
1) Merge API shape PR and publish beta SDK packages.
2) Wire telemetry events into backend.
3) Run canary, iterate on sensitivity defaults based on observed duplicate-rate.

Note: This ticket focuses on cross-SDK ergonomics and observability. Language-specific performance micro-optimizations (zero-copy streams in Go) should be separate follow-ups (see ENG-???)
